title: Exact orders and invariant anticanonical linear systems
main_claim: Setup: X is smooth projective, -K_X = L is smoothly semipositive, and ℓ is the curvature-null functional. Suppose effective N_j ~ m_jL+M with ℓ(N_j)=0 and v(N_j)/m_j → 0, where v is a centered (or zero) valuation. Then there is an effective N ~_Q L with v(N)=0 (Thm 1.1). Consequences: an exact-zero-order corollary for formal arcs, and invariant anticanonical sections for torus actions when H^i(O_X)=0 for i>0 (Thm 1.2).

issues.location: null-field.tex, final paragraphs (application of CompanionG Toroidal volume metric and CompanionE Thm Finite generation near a correction divisor)
issues.description: The k≠C case rests on two companion theorems used as black boxes. One is CompanionG's toroidal volume metric, giving A_0 with f^*A_0 p-exceptional and an integrable semipositive metric on -K_Y+A_0. The other is CompanionE's correction-ring finite generation. I compared the hypotheses as stated and they match: rk g_*O_Z(E_Z)=1 holds by Lemma 3.2, and the horizontal patch lies in g^{-1}(U) minus Supp E_Z. I did not re-audit the companions' proofs. The family board has a no-gap report for CompanionG; CompanionE has none.
issues.evidence: CompanionG Thm (Toroidal volume metric) needs W normal, f equidimensional and toroidal, rank one, and a patch where π^*α ≥ c g^*ω_Y. All of these are verified in Section 3. CompanionE Thm needs a semipositive metric with L^1_loc frame norms that is smooth and strictly positive on an ordinary open set, which is what CompanionG supplies.

coverage: I read every step of the main chain: the introduction, endpoint.tex (Lemma 2.1 and Prop 2.2), null-field.tex, exact-proof.tex, arc-corollary.tex, order-weight.tex and exact-weights.tex (proof of Thm 1.2). I also checked the statements of the CompanionG toroidal-volume theorem and the CompanionE correction-ring theorem (with the proof of its integrable-neighborhood lemma) against how this paper applies them. I verified the following: the valuation-of-sum step that selects a monomial; the bound v(f_j) ≥ λb_j − (C_2+|λ|C_1)a_j; base effectivity P(t_j)+div h_j ≥ 0; horizontal and vertical coefficient effectivity on W, and removal of A by pushforward; closure, relative algebraic closedness and finite generation of the null-polar field; the bpf polar-max argument giving ℓ(π_*g^*H)=0; uniqueness of the rank-one Jacobian section; the pointwise vanishing of the top form, kernel inclusion, and strict patch; the linear system for t_j and t_*, membership h_j ∈ k⊗Q, and the k=C case; the sign of the order/weight lemma (checked on z ↦ tz, giving order 1 = 0−(−1)); the holomorphic Lefschetz coefficient χ(S,(l−1)L|_S); the ℓ(M) ≤ 0 argument via Calabi–Yau, using the b^ν coefficient; the wedge weight (m_j−e)c and order c_M+ec; and the support-function equality and convex-product step. I did not audit the independent methods, controlled-cone, MRC or isometric descent sections, which are not needed for Thms 1.1 and 1.2.
sibling_notes: The board already had no-gap reports for CompanionG (Metric descent, rank 22), the Bounded-metrics paper and the Cohomological-transfer paper. This paper uses CompanionG's toroidal volume metric with exactly the stated hypotheses. CompanionE (Integrable metrics…correction ring) has not been reported in fam 068 yet.
